newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia winter wheat crop seen 16.7 mln T.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia winter wheat crop seen 16.7 mln T.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA: WINTER CROP FORECAST AT 16.7 MLN TONNES (17.1 MLN 1996)
MOSCOW, April 18 - Russian winter wheat output in 1997 is forecast to decline in most areas because of the decrease in acreage sown last autumn.
SovEcon's forecast for Russia's total wheat output is provisionally put at 16.7 million tonnes -- and in a range of 16.0-17.5 million tonnes, down from 17.1 million tonnes in 1996.

Assuming normal crop development, winter wheat yields are anticipated to increase in most areas, particularly in the North Caucasus, where winter wheat output may increase to 8.8 million tonnes, about 1.0 million tonnes up on last year.
But the final outcome of the planting season will depend crucially on weather conditions in the Urals and Siberia, where spring sowing will start in early May.
By April 14, 941,000 hectares in Russia had been sown to spring grains, 74 percent up on the same date last year when the spring campaign lagged well behind a normal pace.
The current spring grain planting progress remains slightly behind normal.
However, reseeded winter plantings area is negligible so far. It accounts for only 1.0 percent of the total area compared with 7.6 percent at the same data last year.
This reflects reduced winterkill losses in the North Caucasus, Russia's wheat belt, in 1997.
Also, soil moisture is currently adequate in major winter grain producing areas (Central Chernozem, Povolzhsk and North Caucasus).
